intent: Stop the endurain importer duplicating runs that RunnerUp uploaded to Endurain directly, and stop its adb fallback silently failing whenever more than one device is attached.
scope: python_pkg/endurain_import/ledger.py — start time parsed from the export filename
python_pkg/endurain_import/upload.py — recent-activity query and start-time comparison
Non-goal: deleting duplicates that already exist. This prevents new ones; it never deletes.
Non-goal: changing the WebDAV inbox or the phone-side files (screen-locker reads the same directory).
changes: sources.py: replaced phone_attached() with attached_serials() + resolve_serial(). The old check returned true when ANY device was in the 'device' state, after which every bare adb call failed with 'more than one device/emulator' as a warning on a path nobody watches. The serial is now threaded into every _adb() call as -s. Ambiguity is resolved by configuration (ENDURAIN_ADB_SERIAL), never by guessing: several devices and no pin means the fallback is skipped outright.

ledger.py: added activity_start(), which parses the run's start time out of the RunnerUp export filename. RunnerUp names exports in LOCAL wall-clock time, so the value is read in the local zone and returned as UTC; reading it as UTC directly shifts a late-evening run onto the wrong day (RunnerUp_2026-08-14-00-58-45 is 2026-08-13 22:58 UTC).

upload.py: added EndurainClient.recent_start_times(), which fetches one page of recent activities and returns their start times, plus already_present() which compares with a +/-120s tolerance. Endurain exposes no query-by-start-time endpoint, so existence is decided client-side. The tolerance exists because the recorded value is not the one in the file: a run whose export embeds 21:51:04Z was stored by Endurain as 21:51:05Z, which exact equality would miss.

upload.py: recent_start_times() returns None (not an empty list) for a transport failure, an auth failure, or an unparseable body, so a failed lookup can never be read as 'no matching activity exists'.

__main__.py: _process() gained a third dedupe check against remote_starts, queried once per run rather than per file. A None result falls back to the existing digest/activity-key ledger checks, which is the previous behaviour. A run matched remotely is recorded in the ledger so the next run skips it without needing the query.

verification.evidence: Ran against the live service with two devices genuinely attached (Pixel 6a 23181JEGR08034 over USB, BL9000 over 192.168.1.131:5555). Logged: '2 devices attached (23181JEGR08034, 192.168.1.131:5555); set ENDURAIN_ADB_SERIAL to choose one. Skipping the phone fallback rather than pulling from an arbitrary device.' Before this change the same situation produced 'could not list /sdcard/Documents/RunnerUp: adb: more than one device/emulator'.

verification.command: python -c 'from python_pkg.endurain_import import sources; sources.resolve_serial()' under three real device configurations
verification.evidence: Two devices attached, no env: None + warning naming both serials. ENDURAIN_ADB_SERIAL=23181JEGR08034: returned '23181JEGR08034'. ENDURAIN_ADB_SERIAL=NOPE123: None + warning that the pinned device is not attached.

verification.command: python -c 'from python_pkg.endurain_import.ledger import activity_start' on real export filenames
verification.evidence: RunnerUp_2026-08-22-23-51-04_Running.tcx -> 2026-08-22 21:51:04+00:00 (DB holds 21:51:05, inside tolerance). RunnerUp_Pixel_6a_2026-08-22-23-51-04_Running.gpx -> identical instant, confirming the device model is stripped. RunnerUp_2026-08-14-00-58-45_Running.tcx -> 2026-08-13 22:58:45+00:00, the day-boundary case. garbage.tcx and RunnerUp_2026-13-45-99-99-99_Running.tcx -> None.

verification.command: python -c 'from python_pkg.endurain_import.upload import already_present' at the tolerance boundary
verification.evidence: 1s skew (the real 14/15 collision) -> True. 120s -> True. 121s -> False. Unrelated run -> False. Empty known list -> False.

verification.command: python -c 'EndurainClient(...).recent_start_times(1)' against the running server with both API keys
verification.evidence: Both keys returned None and logged 'could not list recent activities: 401 (the API key needs the activities:read scope for duplicate detection)'. Confirmed against the DB: both keys hold scopes ["activities:upload"] only. The fail-closed path is therefore exercised end to end; the positive path is covered by unit tests until the scope is granted.
__init__.py, __main__.py (92 stmts, 20 branches), ledger.py (74/12), sources.py (77/30), upload.py (93/20) all at 100% with zero missed branches. No lint suppressions added.

risks: The remote check is inert until the Endurain API key is granted the activities:read scope. Until then recent_start_times() returns None every run and dedupe falls back to the ledger, which is exactly the previous behaviour — no regression, but no new protection either.

A pre-existing duplicate (activities 14 and 15 share a start time) makes Endurain's own get_activity_by_start_time raise MultipleResultsFound, which 500s an upload of THAT run. Other runs are unaffected. This change does not delete duplicates; the collision has to be cleared in the UI.

The +/-120s tolerance would collapse two genuinely distinct runs starting within two minutes of each other into one. Judged not a real scenario for a running log; the alternative (exact match) demonstrably misses the real 1s recording skew.

resolve_serial() now refuses to pull when several devices are attached and no serial is pinned. That is a deliberate behaviour change: the fallback stops silently rather than pulling from an arbitrary device. Set ENDURAIN_ADB_SERIAL to restore pulling.
rollback: git revert the commit; the importer returns to phone_attached() and ledger-only dedupe.

After rollback confirm: systemctl --user start endurain-import.service exits 0, and the ledger at ~/.local/state/endurain-import/ledger.json is unchanged (this change never rewrites existing entries).
No data migration is involved — the ledger format is unchanged and no server state is written by the new code path (it only issues GETs).
